text:
Ana: Hey team — quick coordination thread for Maria (new hire, product eng) who's set to start May 15 but is waiting on consular stamping for H-1B COS. Need to confirm i9 remote option, payroll provisional start, benefits eligibility if stamping slips. @Raj can you confirm manager preference (remote onboarding vs delay)?
Raj: Confirmed manager is fine with a remote-first onboarding for 2–4 weeks. Will manager approve contractor bridging if needed?
Maria: Hi all — consulate gave me an appointment on May 22, earliest return to US May 26. I don't have an EAD. Does that mean I can't start on May 15?
Ana: Thanks Maria. Short answers: 1) We can't put you on payroll as W-2 until work authorization is valid. 2) Remote onboarding (access, trainings) is fine before payroll, but benefits/paid time will follow actual payroll start. 3) We can do an I-9 remote verification if you have an authorized agent in-country — link to steps: https://hr.redwood.example/i9-remote (please upload agent attestation).
Jordan: Payroll note: We can create a "pending start" record with tentative start date in the HRIS so manager can allocate training/headcount, but we won't issue salary until DOJ verification clears. If manager wants the person paid earlier we'd need to onboard them as a contractor (1099/agency) — needs manager + legal approval.
Maria: Is courier for passport back to consulate covered? Also I have a fingerprint/bio appointment clash possibility — what's the contingency?
Ana: Redwood covers expedited courier costs for stamping-related passport shipping. Send receipts to hr-expenses@redwood.com after return and we'll reimburse immediately. If biometrics/fingerprint shifts your appointment, please tell us the new dates; we can adjust provisional start.
ImmigrationBot: Reminder: please upload passport photo page and DS-160 confirmation to the candidate portal: https://immigration.redwood.example/upload. Missing: passport.pdf, ds160.pdf
Raj: Manager prefers remote onboarding and will approve contractor bridging only if there's a hard blocker >2 weeks. I'll get a fast approval path from Legal if needed.
Jordan: Also important — benefits enrollment window: we can allow a delayed enrollment effective date tied to actual payroll start. If start slips past 30 days we may need to re-open enrollment manually. I'll flag benefits ops to watch Maria's file.
Maria: Okay thanks. For i9 agent, I have a notary in my city who can do the verification on May 27 if needed. I'll upload their attestation.
Ana: Perfect. Action items: Raj — confirm contractor approval threshold with manager (by EOD). Jordan — set up pending start in HRIS and note benefits re-open guardrails. Maria — upload passport + DS-160 and notary attestation when available. I'll send courier instructions once stamping is confirmed. :thumbsup:
Raj: Will do.
Maria: Thank you all! Appreciate the clarity.
Ana: Adding checklist link for everyone's reference: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/HR/Consular+Stamping+Checklist. If anything changes ping me.
